name: Acne Vulgaris
description: Acne is a very common skin condition that occurs when hair follicles under the skin become clogged with oil (sebum) and dead skin cells. It causes blackheads, whiteheads, red pimples, and sometimes deeper tender lumps.
common_symptoms: Whiteheads (clogged pores that stay closed beneath the skin)
Blackheads (open clogged pores where surface oil turns dark from oxidation)
Pimples with white or yellow pus at the tips (pustules)
Large, solid, painful lumps deep beneath the skin (nodules or cystic lesions)
Most common on the face, forehead, chest, upper back, and shoulders
causes: Excess oil (sebum) production by skin oil glands
Hair follicles clogged by oil and dead skin cells
Proliferation of Cutibacterium acnes bacteria inside clogged pores
Inflammation and immune response in the pore wall
risk_factors: Hormonal shifts during puberty, menstrual cycles, or pregnancy
Greasy or heavy pore-clogging cosmetics, lotions, or hair pomades
Friction or pressure from helmets, phone screens, tight collars, or backpacks
High glycemic index diets and psychological stress
first_aid: Wash face gently twice a day with a mild, non-drying cleanser
Apply a clean, warm washcloth for 5 minutes to soothe painful pimples
Do not pop, squeeze, or pick at lesions
precautions: Use skincare and makeup products clearly labeled 'non-comedogenic' or 'oil-free'
Wash your face gently with fingertips, avoiding harsh loofahs or abrasive scrubs
Shampoo your hair regularly if you have oily hair to prevent forehead breakouts
Keep phone screens and pillowcases clean
home_care: Wash face twice daily with lukewarm water and a gentle cleanser
Apply gentle over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid gel consistently
Allow 6 to 8 weeks for acne products to show visible improvement
do_not: DO NOT squeeze, pop, or needle pimples, which forces bacteria deeper and causes scarring and dark spots
DO NOT scrub skin aggressively, which irritates skin and worsens acne
DO NOT apply toothpaste, lemon juice, or household baking soda to skin lesions
DO NOT touch or pick your face throughout the day
red_flags: Deep, painful, large cysts or nodules that can cause permanent pitted scarring
Sudden severe inflammatory acne eruption with joint pain and fever (acne fulminans)
Severe emotional distress, depression, or anxiety related to skin appearance
when_to_see_doctor: See a dermatologist or doctor if over-the-counter acne products do not improve your skin after 8 to 12 weeks, or if you have deep, painful cystic bumps that cause scars.
prevention: Wash face morning, evening, and after heavy sweating
Always choose oil-free and non-comedogenic cosmetics and moisturizers
Remove all makeup thoroughly before going to sleep
